entities.summary:
Pavle Đurišić was a Montenegrin Serb regular officer of the Royal Yugoslav Army who became a Chetnik commander (vojvoda) and led a significant proportion of the Chetniks in Montenegro during World War II. He distinguished himself and became one of the main commanders during the popular uprising against the Italians in Montenegro in July 1941, but later collaborated with the Italians in actions against the Communist-led Yugoslav Partisans. In 1943, his troops carried out several massacres against the Serbian Orthodox population in Montenegro.


Pavle Đurišić played a pivotal role in the Chetnik movement, leading his troops in numerous battles against the Partisans and collaborating with the Italians. His actions had far-reaching consequences, contributing to the escalation of violence and sectarian tensions in post-war Yugoslavia. The Đurišić massacre, in which his troops killed hundreds of Serbian Orthodox civilians, remains a dark chapter in Montenegrin history.


The legacy of Pavle Đurišić is complex and contested. While some view him as a national hero for his role in the Chetnik movement, others condemn his collaboration with the Italians and his role in the Đurišić massacre. Today, Đurišić is remembered primarily as a symbol of the violent and divisive legacy of Yugoslavia's complex history.

entities.summary:
Pavle Đurišić was a Montenegrin Serb regular officer of the Royal Yugoslav Army who became a Chetnik commander (vojvoda) and led a significant proportion of the Chetniks in Montenegro during World War II.

As a key figure in the popular uprising against the Italians in Montenegro in July 1941, Đurišić distinguished himself and became one of the main commanders of the Chetniks during this period.

However, in 1943, his troops carried out several massacres against the Communist-led Yugoslav Partisans, marking a significant turning point in Đurišić's collaboration with the Italian forces.

Today, Pavle Đurišić is remembered as a complex figure in Montenegrin history, embodying both the nationalist fervor of the Chetniks and the brutal realities of war.

Pavle Đurišić was born on July 9, 1909, in Podgorica, Montenegro, and died on April 21, 1945.
